papers.title: Obeticholic acid as second-line therapy for primary biliary cholangitis: Does target trial emulation solve the issue?
papers.one_line: A component-by-component audit of a published emulation finds that follow-up begins at first dose for treated patients and at cohort entry for controls, so time survived before treatment is unbalanced, while the disease phenotype rests on codes with a positive predictive value of only 70% to 75%.
papers.what_was_done: An editorial audit of the HEROES emulation of obeticholic acid versus no second-line treatment in primary biliary cholangitis, conducted against the seven target trial components. The emulated results were a weighted as-treated hazard ratio of 0.37 (95% CI 0.14 to 0.75), a first intention-to-treat analogue of 0.59 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.995) removing censoring at discontinuation, and a second intention-to-treat analogue of 0.64 (95% CI 0.38 to 1.05) accounting for crossover, against the confirmatory COBALT trial's hazard ratio of 1.01 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.51). The cohort was drawn from a claims database linked to laboratory, transplant and vital status data. Identified defects: disease codes with positive predictive value of 70% to 75%; an unvalidated pharmacy-fill algorithm for ursodeoxycholic acid nonresponse, with 40% of initiators having alkaline phosphatase below 1.67 times the upper limit of normal and the corresponding proportion among controls unreported; a propensity score containing mainly liver-related variables plus the Charlson index, omitting provider characteristics and time-varying confounders; no outcome control; and unvalidated hospitalization codes for the outcome that drove the composite. The proposed remedy is risk-set matching of each treated patient at first eligible visit to controls with equal time since enrollment, with inverse probability of censoring weights for later initiators.

future_research.gap: Whether the drug improves clinical outcomes remains undetermined after both the trial and the emulation.
future_research.quote: Given the primary findings and limitations of the HEROES target trial, it remains uncertain whether second-line OCA improves clinical outcomes in PBC.

problems.evidence: Follow-up starts at first dose for the treated and at the eligible visit for controls, so treated patients bring in survival time accrued between cohort entry and initiation that controls do not have. No outcome-blind rule chose that grid, and the reported as-treated hazard ratio of 0.37 is precisely the estimate such an asymmetry inflates; the correction offered is a matched design that forces time previously survived to be equal.
problems.quote: Thus, the time survived from enrollment is not balanced for the OCA and control groups, as patients with OCA have a certain length of time survived between cohort entry and treatment initiation, while the control patients do not.

problems.evidence: The disease phenotype is a claims code set with a positive predictive value of 70% to 75%, entered as if it were error free, and the misclassification is expected to be differential: patients without the disease are more likely to sit in the untreated arm because treatment is itself a marker of true disease. The adjustment set, built mainly from liver variables, cannot correct for a comparator arm that partly does not have the condition.
problems.quote: The HEROES study uses International Classification of Diseases codes to identify patients with PBC, which have a positive predictive value of only 70%–75%, likely leading to the inclusion of patients without PBC, an issue that would be anticipated to occur more often in the non-OCA group.

problems.evidence: Insufficient response or intolerance to first-line therapy is the eligibility criterion, and it is reconstructed from a pharmacy fill algorithm that has never been checked against charts. The consequence is measurable: 40% of initiators had alkaline phosphatase below the threshold that defines second-line candidacy, so a criterion that was not met is indistinguishable in the data from one that was, and the proportion among controls is not reported at all.
problems.quote: This may explain why 40% of OCAinitiating patients (and an unreported percent of controls) had ALP < 1.67 times the upper limit of normal, below the threshold used for second-line therapy in the original trials.

problems.evidence: A negative control outcome is named as the missing step: an endpoint on which the drug should have no effect would have revealed residual confounding in a propensity score that omitted provider characteristics and every time-varying variable. That such a control was warranted and simply not run shows negative controls are not a required part of the workflow, only something a reviewer notices afterward.
problems.quote: Further analyses to assess for residual confounding were also warranted but not performed, such as the use of an outcome control (ie, an outcome for which no causal effect of OCA would be expected).

problems.evidence: Restricting decompensation to hospitalized events makes the outcome definition interact with the treatment protocol: portal hypertension signs that arise earlier are a contraindication, so the drug is stopped before the event can be captured, and the as-treated analysis then never observes it. Outcome ascertainment is here an identifying choice rather than a definition, and transplant waitlisting, the more proximal failure event, was left out of the composite.
problems.quote: This could result in OCA being discontinued well before there was an opportunity to capture hospitalization for decompensation in the “as treated” analysis, erroneously overestimating perceived benefit.

problems.evidence: An analysis carrying the target trial label produced hazard ratios from 0.37 to 0.64 while the confirmatory trial reported 1.01 (95% CI 0.68 to 1.51), and it took a component-by-component audit to expose the misaligned time zero, the unvalidated phenotype and the incomplete adjustment set. The framework's name is shown to carry no information about the assumption burden actually incurred.
problems.quote: However, if protocol components are incorrectly specified and/or the analysis plan is incomplete, significant biases can occur and yield erroneous results.

problems.evidence: The two intention-to-treat analogues moved from 0.59 (95% CI 0.34 to 0.995) to 0.64 (95% CI 0.38 to 1.05) once crossover to the drug in the comparator arm was accounted for, and crossover to commercially available drug was already a documented failure mode of the confirmatory trial. The attenuation is treated as an analysis variant rather than as a property of the estimand that grows with follow-up.
problems.quote: a first intent-to-treat analysis with HR 0.59 (95% CI: 0.34–0.995) that eliminated censoring at OCA discontinuation and a second intent-to-treat analysis with HR 0.64 (95% CI: 0.38–1.05) that accounted for treatment crossover

papers.title: External comparator studies and the joint application of the estimand and target trial emulation frameworks.
papers.one_line: Mapping the five ICH E9(R1) estimand attributes onto the seven target trial components yields nine mutually exclusive unifying elements, two of which (baseline and the marginal estimator) belong to neither framework as published.
papers.what_was_done: A conceptual reconciliation of the estimand framework and the target trial emulation framework for external comparator studies, where a single-arm trial is contextualized against observational comparator data. The five estimand attributes (treatment, population, endpoint, intercurrent events, population-level summary) and the seven target trial components (eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, assignment procedures, follow-up period, outcomes, causal contrasts, data analysis plan) are combined into nine unifying elements, of which element 7 (baseline) and element 9 (the marginal estimator, meaning the choice among ATE, ATT, ATU and ATO) appear in neither framework. The estimand framework is shown to be silent on outcome misclassification, on data quality and on the definition of time zero; the target trial framework is shown to be silent on the five estimand strategies for intercurrent events, so that its use of the term intention-to-treat is ambiguous. No empirical study, no data and no effect estimates are reported. The proposal is offered against two named prior attempts that each laid out the two frameworks differently for one case study, with no agreed structure between them.

future_research.gap: How the two overlapping frameworks should be jointly structured is unsettled and offered only as a first step.
future_research.quote: However, our proposal can only be seen as a first step to initiating a thorough scientific discussion, and we welcome further contributions that debate how to structure the joint application of the two overlapping frameworks of estimands and target trial emulation in the best possible way.

problems.evidence: External comparator studies are shown to lack the recorded quantity that defines the trial estimand: intention to treat cannot be reconstructed because the data record dispensing rather than intent. What is estimated is therefore an intention-to-treat analogue defined by the data source, not a noisy measurement of the trial's intention-to-treat effect, and the two are not distinguished by name. The framework mapping treats this as an emulation limitation rather than as a change of estimand.
problems.quote: The classic clinical trial approach of assessing treatments is based on the intention-to-treat population, which is usually not available in EC studies because it is typically not recorded which patients were intended to be treated but just which patients have actually received treatment.

problems.evidence: Nine unifying elements are derived, yet no accounting is proposed that would say how much of the gap between the scientific target and the reported estimate is attributable to each element. Two independent published attempts to lay the frameworks side by side for a single study produced two different structures, and diversity is expected to grow. Structure without a decomposition leaves the loss unpartitioned.
problems.quote: This joint application should happen in a structured and standardized manner, which does not seem to be available currently.

problems.evidence: Data quality enters only under assignment procedures, as a checklist of sub-categories (missingness, mismeasurement, misclassification, fitness for purpose) with no threshold attached to any of them. The proposal notes that the estimand framework omits data quality entirely because quality bears on the estimate rather than the estimand, so nothing in either framework can stop a study on data-fitness grounds.
problems.quote: Granular sub-categories of data quality may be defined, including missingness and accuracy considerations (mismeasurement and misclassification), and whether the data is generally fit for purpose

problems.evidence: Outcome misclassification is placed inside the target trial framework and absent from the estimand framework, and the remedy offered is a naming convention: prefix the observational endpoint with real-world so that a difference in measurement accuracy shows on the estimand level. Renaming rwPFS against PFS records that error may differ; it does not quantify it or propagate it into the estimate.
problems.quote: The EF, however, does not address outcome misclassification and validation approaches.
problems.locator: 2.3 EF attribute #3 endpoint and TTEF component #5 outcome

problems.evidence: The population-level summary is treated as a free choice made late, and the hazard ratio is flagged as a poor one because proportional hazards becomes fragile when two data sources are mixed. Nothing in either framework prevents an external comparator study from reporting a hazard ratio when the specified estimand was something else, and the marginal estimator (ATE, ATT, ATU or ATO) is not part of either framework at all.
problems.quote: For example, the hazard ratio may not be the best population-level summary because the underlying assumption of proportional hazards is likely to become fragile when mixing different data sources.

problems.evidence: Overlap weighting is presented as a fourth marginal estimator that shifts the target to patients in clinical equipoise, alongside ATE, ATT and ATU. The choice is framed as a stakeholder preference to be negotiated before the protocol is final, not as a diagnostic that reports which patient histories the comparator data cannot support. The ATE is criticized for depending on the sample size ratio of the two cohorts, which is an artifact of nonoverlap that no positivity diagnostic is asked to name.
problems.quote: The ATO derives a marginal estimator by comparing patients who are in clinical equipoise
problems.locator: 2.9 EF further consideration #9 the marginal estimator

problems.evidence: Regulatory bodies are cited as requiring both frameworks for external comparator studies, but the resolution of the choice that most changes the answer, which marginal estimator to target, is left to case-by-case consultation before protocol finalization. No threshold, default or acceptance criterion is available from either the estimand framework or the target trial framework.
problems.quote: Regulatory or HTA stakeholder input should be sought before finalizing the EC study protocol to ensure that external preferences or requirements are met, and more than one marginal estimator could be specified as supplementary analyses.
problems.locator: 2.9 EF further consideration #9 the marginal estimator

papers.title: Review of the target trial methodological approach on treatment effect estimates in kidney failure: protocol for a systematic assessment.
papers.one_line: A protocol for a methodological review of emulations in kidney failure states that reporting bias cannot be assessed because no registration requirement exists for trial emulation studies.
papers.what_was_done: A PRISMA-P protocol for a methodological systematic review of studies using the whole or part of the target trial approach in late-stage chronic kidney disease and kidney failure, searching MEDLINE and Embase to 1 July 2023 plus backward citation chasing, restricted to English and German full-text publications on therapeutic interventions with patient-relevant clinical outcomes. Full-text screening applies a five-domain checklist to decide whether a study counts as a target trial emulation at all: indication, causal research question, prespecified target trial criteria, time zero, and emulation. Quality of reporting is assessed with RECORD-PE and risk of bias with an adapted ROBINS-I instrument. Three questions are set: whether the design is valid, whether the emulation is well conducted, and whether the effect estimate is robust, each defined by a narrative criterion rather than a threshold. The stated plan is to identify at what stage studies failed and to publish specific examples of the most common points of failure. No publication bias assessment is planned, and reporting bias assessment is declared limited because trial emulation studies are not required to be registered. No results are reported; the review had not been conducted.

future_research.gap: Methodological guidance specific to emulation in kidney failure does not exist and is the intended product of the review.
future_research.quote: We will provide specific methodological recommendations on how to design target trials and model assumptions for emulation to get reliable treatment effect estimates for therapeutic interventions in kidney failure.

problems.evidence: A review team that set out to assess reporting bias across emulations in one clinical area concluded it could not, because no registry holds emulation protocols. Nothing records which protocol versions were tried and discarded before the published one, and the review's own workaround, checking appendices and online registration databases for outcome switching, is stated to be incomplete for exactly that reason.
problems.quote: However, given there is no requirement for registration of trial emulation studies, comprehensive examination of reporting bias will be limited.

problems.evidence: The review has to build a five-domain screening checklist just to decide which self-described studies are emulations, and it plans to compare studies that qualify against studies that used the label without meeting the criteria. That such a triage step is necessary at the screening stage establishes that the label is applied independently of whether the design carries the assumption burden it implies.
problems.quote: Full-text review will be based on a checklist in which across five domains we will assess whether the study can be defined as target trial emulation study.
problems.locator: Information sources, search strategy, and study selection

problems.evidence: The three appraisal questions are resolved by narrative criteria: the design is valid if a specific target trial with an appropriate causal question was defined, the emulation is well conducted if the dataset is robust enough and time zero is synchronized, and the estimate is robust if matching was appropriate and sensitivity analyses were performed. None of the three carries a numeric threshold, so no study can fail on stated grounds; the review must construct its own acceptance criteria because the field supplies none.
problems.quote: The emulation is well conducted if the dataset is robust enough for the emulation and eligibility, and timepoint 0 and the start of follow-up are synchronized.

problems.evidence: Data fitness enters the appraisal as the phrase robust enough for the emulation, applied by two reviewers with a third resolving disagreement. There is no measurement of fitness and no point at which a data source would be declared unusable, so the same narrative judgment that the review is auditing is the instrument used to audit it.
problems.quote: Target trial emulation is a sophisticated technique for testing causal inference in non-randomized studies by systematically eliminating inadvertent and unnecessary biases.

problems.evidence: Kidney failure is chosen precisely because these patients are excluded from trials, so almost no emulation in this area will have a trial to be checked against. Confidence has to be transferred from emulations that succeeded elsewhere, and the review's premise is a general claim that emulation results resemble trustworthy results more closely than traditional observational studies, with no theory saying which features of the successful cases carry over to dialysis and transplantation questions.
problems.quote: As such, results of target trial emulation have repeatedly been shown to resemble more closely trustworthy and reliable results than traditional observational studies

papers.title: Going beyond randomised controlled trials to assess treatment effect heterogeneity across target populations.
papers.one_line: Emulating a target trial in 13,240 CPRD patients with a local instrumental variable, the analysis assuming no unobserved confounding gave average treatment effects in the opposite direction to the instrumental variable estimates yet still met the benchmark criterion of estimate agreement with the reference trial.
papers.what_was_done: A target trial emulation in the Clinical Practice Research Datalink comparing DPP4 inhibitors with sulfonylureas as second-line therapy for type 2 diabetes, using regional prescribing variation across 162 clinical commissioning groups as an instrument for a local instrumental variable estimator of individualized treatment effects. The target population was 13,240 people defined by national guideline eligibility, split into an RCT-eligible subpopulation (n = 6497) matching a published trial's criteria and an RCT-ineligible subpopulation (n = 6743). Individualized effects on one-year change in HbA1c were aggregated to average and conditional average treatment effects. For the RCT-eligible group the estimated average effects matched the published trial; for the stratum with baseline HbA1c at or above 88 mmol/mol the difference favored DPP4 inhibitors by 5.3 mmol/mol with an interval of minus 12.8 to 2.2. Conditional effects agreed in direction between eligible and ineligible subpopulations but differed in magnitude, and the spread of individualized effects was wider among the ineligible. A comparison analysis using inverse probability weighting with regression adjustment produced average effects of opposite sign to the instrumental variable estimates. Prior simulation work is cited as requiring an instrument F statistic above 100 and sample size above 5000 for the method to be consistent.

future_research.gap: Heterogeneity in populations excluded from trials has been studied in one clinical scenario and needs settings where the trial is nested in the same data.
future_research.quote: Future research is required to explore HTE in populations explicitly excluded from RCTs, across a broader array of settings including those where the RCT is nested within the EHR data to allow this aspect of selection to be formally studied.

future_research.gap: Local instrumental variable methods do not yet deliver conditional effects for specific comparisons when more than two treatments are of interest.
future_research.quote: In settings, where more than two treatment comparators are of interest, further development of the requisite LIV methods are required as current approaches identify the marginal treatment effect of a treatment versus the next best alternative

problems.evidence: Two estimators disagreed on the sign of the average treatment effect, and both passed the same replication test because the criterion is whether a point estimate falls inside the reference trial's interval. A binary agreement label is shown here to be insensitive to a sign reversal in the underlying estimand, which is the strongest available demonstration that the label is not a calibrated comparison.
problems.quote: The alternative analysis assuming no unobserved confounding provided estimates of ATEs that were in the opposite direction to those from the LIV, but for the ‘RCT‐eligible’ population still met the criteria for ‘estimate agreement’ with those from Nauck et al.

problems.evidence: The same 13,240-person cohort analyzed with a local instrumental variable and with inverse probability weighting plus regression adjustment produced average effects of opposite sign and conditional effects that differed in the ineligible subpopulation. Neither estimator was required to demonstrate in advance that its choice mattered, and the recommendation offered is prospective advice to prefer instrumental variable approaches rather than a diagnostic that a study must report.
problems.quote: Future target trial approaches should consider LIV approaches that can address both confounding and heterogeneity, and avoid relying on methods that assume no unobserved confounding and no essential heterogeneity, especially when a valid instrument is available and interest lies in broader populations for which there is no RCT benchmark.

problems.evidence: The subgroups whose conditional effects diverged most from the trial benchmark are exactly the ones excluded from the trial: people with baseline HbA1c at or above 88 mmol/mol and obesity classes 2 and 3, where between-treatment imbalance was largest. The clinically significant subgroup effect (a 5.3 mmol/mol improvement) carries an interval from minus 12.8 to 2.2, so the subgroup with the worst overlap is also the one whose effect is least identified.
problems.quote: As anticipated, baseline imbalances were more pronounced for the ‘RCT‐ineligible’ subpopulation, with large between‐treatment differences in the proportions with HbA1C ≥ 88 and in the proportions in Obesity Classes 2 and 3.

problems.evidence: Transporting a trial estimate to this target population requires that no unobserved variable both drives trial selection and modifies the effect. The excluded characteristics here (poor glycemic control, older age) are correlated with diet, adherence and frailty, none of which are recorded in either the trial or the electronic health record, so the transport assumption is added on top of the confounding assumption with no separate accounting of either.
problems.quote: This extant literature has made the common crucial assumption, that there is no essential heterogeneity, which can also be expressed as no trial selection according to unobserved variables that modify the relative treatment effect.

problems.evidence: Partitioning the guideline-defined target population into an RCT-eligible subpopulation (n = 6497) and an RCT-ineligible one (n = 6743) and reporting effects in each isolates one component of the gap between the scientific target and the trial estimand: mismatch attributable to eligibility. It does not separate protocol compromise, mapping loss or estimation error, and the residual spread of individualized effects within each partition is left unattributed.
problems.quote: We identified 13,240 people from 162 CCGs in the CPRD data who met the inclusion criteria for the target population.

problems.evidence: Even with a strong instrument and more than 13,000 people, the effects that incorporate unobserved heterogeneity remain imprecise, and 135 individualized effects (1% of the population) fell outside a range of minus 20 to 20 mmol/mol and were dropped from display. Nothing in the reporting names which covariate histories those unstable individualized effects belong to.
problems.quote: Fourth, in our example, we had a strong IV and moderately large sample size, but the LIV estimates that incorporated essential heterogeneity were still somewhat imprecise.

papers.title: Target Trial Emulation for Evaluating Health Policy.
papers.one_line: A seven-component policy trial emulation framework splits units into policy level and impact level and concedes that a bundle of simultaneously implemented policies cannot be decomposed into individual effects unless each affects distinct unrelated outcomes.
papers.what_was_done: A methodological adaptation of target trial emulation to health policy evaluation, where policies are adopted by states, cities or organizations rather than assigned to individuals. The framework has seven components: units and eligibility criteria, definitions of exposure and comparison conditions, assignment mechanism, baseline and follow-up, outcomes, causal estimand, and statistical analysis and assumptions. Units are separated into policy-level units that could implement the policy and impact-level sub-units whose outcomes are measured, so the emulation is of a cluster-randomized rather than an individually randomized trial. Exposure definition is handled by policy mapping or legal epidemiology to identify versions and core components, with medical cannabis laws given as a case where the qualifying conditions vary by state and over time; where heterogeneity is high a multi-arm trial with multiple exposure versions is proposed. Staggered adoption is handled by stacking, meaning one emulation per implementation date, aligned at their respective time zeros. Three estimands are distinguished (ATE, ATT, ATC), with the ATT identified as the conventional target. Crossover by comparison units that later adopt the policy is discussed against the historical practice of restricting to never-exposed comparators, which conditions on post-exposure information. Difference-in-differences is treated as the worked analytic method, resting on counterfactual parallel trends, which is stated to be untestable. Censoring weights are noted to be hard to implement with fewer than about 50 units.

future_research.gap: No reporting guideline exists for policy trial emulation and none of the diagnostics needed to evaluate one have been developed.
future_research.quote: Additionally, visualization techniques and diagnostics to describe and evaluate target trial emulations for policy evaluation are needed.

problems.evidence: The assignment unit problem is solved explicitly: policy-level units are the ones that would be randomized, impact-level sub-units are where outcomes are measured, and the emulation is stated to be of a cluster-randomized trial. The treatment version problem is named but not closed. Policy mapping is offered to identify which versions are comparable, and a bundle of near-simultaneous policies is conceded to be undecomposable except in the special case where each policy affects distinct unrelated outcomes.
problems.quote: In such cases, it is typically impossible to estimate effects for each policy in the bundle, unless each policy affects distinct, unrelated outcomes (19,20).
problems.locator: Component 2: Definitions of Exposure and Comparison Conditions

problems.evidence: Each implementing unit adopts the policy idiosyncratically, with medical cannabis laws differing across states and over time in which conditions qualify. The remedy offered is a procedure for describing versions, legal epidemiology, plus the advice that a carefully defined exposure refers to a group of qualitatively similar policies. Which versions belong in the same class remains a judgment; no criterion determines when two policies are the same treatment.
problems.quote: Policy mapping or “legal epidemiology” techniques, which provide a systematic approach to understanding policies’ timing and their granular details, can aid researchers in understanding different versions and core components of the policy of interest, and which of those versions are comparable (18).
problems.locator: Component 2: Definitions of Exposure and Comparison Conditions

problems.evidence: Spillover between policy units is acknowledged as a live threat and enters only as a design tradeoff: near-neighbor comparators such as bordering states are more similar, geographically distant comparators reduce spillover, and the investigator picks one. No interference structure is specified and no estimand is defined under interference, so the choice of comparator distance silently determines which no-interference assumption the estimate requires.
problems.quote: Alternatively, selecting comparators geographically distant from exposed units can alleviate concerns about policy spillover (22).

problems.evidence: Baseline is set at when the policy could start affecting outcomes, and misspecification biases in one direction if set too late (anticipation) and attenuates if set too early. For comparison units, when they could have implemented the policy but did not, the paper states the problem is challenging and offers stacking as a construction rather than a selection rule. Nothing in the framework chooses the date without reference to the outcome series.
problems.quote: Misspecifying baseline might introduce bias due to anticipation effects (if specified too late) or could attenuate the effect estimate (if specified too early).
problems.locator: Component 4: Baseline / Time Zero and Follow-Up

problems.evidence: Stacked difference-in-differences builds one emulation per implementation date and averages the unit-specific effects, so the same comparison units appear in several emulations at different calendar times. The framework states the averaging should happen if scientifically appropriate but supplies no account of the repeated participation this creates, and separately notes that censoring weights are hard to implement with fewer than about 50 units, which is the regime stacking operates in.
problems.quote: Under staggered policy adoption, “stacked” DiD uses serial per-implementationdate trial emulations to estimate unit-specific effects, then averages them if scientifically appropriate (see Figure 1, panels 4–5) (11,24).

problems.evidence: Counterfactual parallel trends is identified as untestable and hard to assess, and the recommended response is that a well-reported emulation will discuss its plausibility so readers can calibrate trust. Diagnosable properties such as pre-policy balance and undiagnosable ones such as parallel trends are therefore delivered through the same narrative channel, and the paper itself records that the diagnostics needed to evaluate a policy emulation do not exist.
problems.quote: The parallel trends assumption is about counterfactuals and is thus untestable and potentially challenging to assess (39).

problems.evidence: Restricting to impact-level units continuously present in the data over the whole study period is offered to keep sample composition fixed, with the tradeoff stated as external validity against internal validity. Presence in an administrative or claims series is itself a healthcare-use variable, so the restriction conditions on a post-baseline process whenever policy adoption is related to who stays in the data, which the framework acknowledges as a possibility requiring care but not as a collider.
problems.quote: If it is unlikely that policy implementation (or lack thereof) is related to impact-level units’ presence or absence in the data over time, we may restrict the sample to units continuously present in the data over the whole study period to avoid changes in sample composition over time.

papers.title: The perpetual need of randomized clinical trials: challenges and uncertainties in emulating the REDUCE-AMI trial.
papers.one_line: A prospectively benchmarked emulation in SWEDEHEART reported hazard ratios of 0.69 to 0.78 for beta-blockers after myocardial infarction while the simultaneously published randomized trial reported 0.96 (95% CI 0.79 to 1.16), a discrepancy the commentary reads as a failed benchmark despite both being non-significant.
papers.what_was_done: A commentary comparing a prospectively benchmarked target trial emulation with the randomized trial it was designed to reproduce. The emulation screened 32,550 SWEDEHEART patients with preserved ejection fraction after recent myocardial infarction, excluded 21,624 who met at least one trial exclusion criterion, and analyzed 10,926, of whom 89.0% received a beta-blocker and 11.0% did not. Over a median 3.4 years in the treated and 3.0 years in the untreated, 10.2% versus 11.9% experienced death or recurrent infarction, giving intention-to-treat hazard ratios from 0.69 (95% CI 0.51 to 0.99) to 0.78 (95% CI 0.59 to 1.12) depending on the maximum follow-up. The trial randomized 5,020 patients, was powered for a hazard ratio of 0.75 at 80% power requiring 379 events, observed 407 events, and reported 7.9% versus 8.3% with a hazard ratio of 0.96 (95% CI 0.79 to 1.16, P = 0.64). Only 88 primary endpoints occurred in the untreated arm of the emulation, so the emulation was underpowered in hindsight. The confounders named as driving beta-blocker prescription and outcome, resting heart rate, blood pressure, residual coronary lesions and anatomy, residual angina, conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias during admission, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, peripheral arterial disease and migraine, are argued to be unrecordable at the needed granularity.

future_research.gap: Emulations are not held to the registration and analysis-plan standards applied to trials.
future_research.quote: We agree, and would like to further argue that TTEs need to be subject to the same level of scrutiny as RCTs, including prospective registration of TTEs and publication of the statistical analysis plans (including a power calculation) [8, 9].

future_research.gap: No reporting exists on how well a weighting or propensity procedure actually explains treatment receipt, as opposed to whether tables look balanced.
future_research.quote: Not just by comparing baseline characteristics (e.g. age, sex, traditional cardiovascular factors) in a table, but quantify how well the characteristics used to facilitate the comparison (e.g. inverse probability weighting or propensity scores,) actually explain the probability whether a given individual would receive the intervention or control treatment.

problems.evidence: Even a successful benchmark here would license nothing beyond this question, because the confounder set is specific to the intervention and outcome pair. The argument is explicit that each intervention and outcome combination has its own confounders, so agreement on beta-blockers after infarction cannot be extrapolated, and in the absence of the trial there is no way to know whether an emulation is unbiased.
problems.quote: Good performance of the REDUCE-AMI TTE compared to the RCT will have limited transportability to other clinical questions, as each intervention and outcome combination has its own set of potential confounders.
problems.locator: Why we need randomized clinical trials

problems.evidence: Read as a binary label, the emulation and the trial agreed, since neither reached significance on the composite endpoint. Read as a comparison of estimands, they disagreed materially: a hazard ratio of 0.96 against 0.69 to 0.78 is the difference between no effect and a 22% to 31% risk reduction that would change practice. With only 88 endpoints in the untreated arm the emulation lacked power to distinguish those, and the binary reading hides both the point-estimate gap and the precision gap.
problems.quote: Whereas the RCT yielded a hazard ratio of 0.96, indicating no signs of efficacy, the TTE yielded hazard ratios of 0.69 to 0.78, corresponding to a 22–31% reduction in death or recurrent myocardial infarction, a clinically relevant and likely practice-changing benefit.
problems.locator: Comparing the REDUCE-AMI trial emulation to the randomized trial

problems.evidence: Prospective benchmarking is presented as necessary precisely because analysis choices can otherwise be tuned until they match a known trial result, and the proposed fix is registration plus published analysis plans including a power calculation. That an emulation's protocol is currently fixed after the data are in hand, and that its confounder set can be selected by the data, is stated as the reason the practice needs to change.
problems.quote: Prospective TTE registration will facilitate insights into potential publication bias, whereas availability of statistical analysis plans will actually ensure the TTE results are not a product of data-driven selection and modelling of potential confounders.

problems.evidence: The call is for prospective registration of emulations because none currently exists, which means the rejected protocol versions and the confounder specifications that were tried and abandoned leave no record. The concrete concern raised, data-driven selection and modeling of potential confounders in a cohort where 89% of patients were treated, is exactly what an unrecorded alternative protocol would conceal.
problems.quote: In order to enhance credibility, trial emulations would benefit from prospective registration, publication of statistical analysis plans, and subsequent prospective benchmarking to randomized clinical trials prior to their publication.

problems.evidence: Screening 32,550 registry patients produced 10,926 analyzable, but the comparator arm held only 11.0% of them and generated 88 primary endpoints, against 407 in the trial. The registry size is not the quantity that determines what the emulation could detect; the untreated arm is, and no power calculation was reported before the analysis.
problems.quote: However, it should be noted that in the TTE only 1 in 9 patients did not use a beta-blocker and only 88 primary end-points were observed in these patients.
problems.locator: Comparing the REDUCE-AMI trial emulation to the randomized trial

problems.evidence: What is asked for is a quantitative report of how well the balancing procedure explains who actually received the drug, rather than a baseline table. Balance in a table is diagnosable and is reported; whether the recorded variables span the prescribing decision is not diagnosable and is not reported, and the two are currently presented to readers as if they were the same evidence.
problems.quote: Groups may be balanced by a substantial number of known factors, but it is not unlikely that other unknown or less well-captured factors have a far greater impact on a clinicians decision to administer the intervention, as discussed above in the case of REDUCE-AMI.

problems.evidence: The confounders named as decisive are a joint set: resting heart rate, blood pressure, residual coronary anatomy, residual angina, conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias during admission, and comorbidities including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, peripheral arterial disease and migraine, each acting on both prescription and prognosis at once. A sensitivity analysis that moves one of them cannot represent a prescribing decision that integrates all of them, which is the reason the commentary concludes the adjustment cannot be done at all.
problems.quote: The case of beta-blockers after myocardial infarction highlights the complexity accounting for factors that feed into clinical decision making

papers.title: Personalized Timing for Allogeneic Stem-Cell Transplantation in Hematologic Neoplasms: A Target Trial Emulation Approach Using Multistate Modeling and Microsimulation.
papers.one_line: No text of this record was retrieved: the cached full text is a different JCO article that cites this work as its reference 23, so nothing in it can be attributed to this DOI.
papers.what_was_done: Retrieval for this record resolved to Tentori et al., a Journal of Clinical Oncology report of a clinical and genomic decision support system for transplant timing in myelodysplastic syndromes, which lists the present work as reference 23. The two are distinct publications in distinct journals. Europe PMC reports the record as closed access with no PMC identifier, so no full text is available. Six findings previously written against this identifier described the Journal of Clinical Oncology article and were removed, because evidence attributed to the wrong publication is worse than no evidence. The record is retained as read with no findings so that the paper count stays honest and the gap is visible.

papers.title: The Inflation Reduction Act: An Opportunity to Accelerate Confidence in Real-World Evidence in the United States.
papers.one_line: A commentary positioning target trial emulation and quantitative bias analysis as the evidence-generation route for Medicare price negotiation states that quantitative bias analysis should only be used when one or two important bias sources exist.
papers.what_was_done: A commentary on what the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act implies for real-world evidence in the United States, given that from 2026 the Secretary of Health and Human Services must weigh comparative effectiveness when negotiating a maximum fair price for selected drugs several years after launch. Target trial emulation is presented as the design framework, strongest when combined with the estimand framework, with a decision flowchart routing from the comparative question through data availability to cloning, censoring and weighting when time zero is not unique, or sequential emulation when several eligibility times exist. Etanercept is used as the worked case, approved across rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, juvenile idiopathic arthritis, plaque psoriasis and ankylosing spondylitis, where trials covering every indication and every competitor are declared infeasible. Quantitative bias analysis is surveyed as external bias adjustment under a Bayesian framework, tipping-point analysis including delta-adjusted pattern imputation, and E-values, each with stated weaknesses: external adjustment is resource intensive and depends on external information, tipping points are hard to judge for plausibility, and E-values are criticized for interpretability and oversimplified assumptions. The stated position is that it remains genuinely uncertain how much the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services will weigh real-world evidence in price negotiation.

future_research.gap: How much weight the payer will place on real-world evidence in price negotiation is undetermined.
future_research.quote: There is genuine uncertainty regarding how much the CMS will value RWE during drug price negotiations.

problems.evidence: The stated scope condition for quantitative bias analysis is that only one or two important bias sources exist, which is a concession that the available machinery does not handle simultaneous violations. The same discussion lists unmeasured confounding, missing smoking status in cancer registries, measurement error and selection bias as routinely co-present in the data these emulations would use, so the recommended tools are declared inapplicable in exactly the setting they are recommended for.
problems.quote: QBA may not be useful if there is a high degree of uncertainty; to begin with, it should only be used if 1 or 2 important sources of bias exist.
problems.locator: Applying QBA to Handle Inherent Limitations of RWD

problems.evidence: A statute that requires comparative effectiveness to be weighed in price setting arrives with no stated standard for what counts as an adequate emulation or an acceptable level of residual confounding, and the commentary's practical advice is early and ongoing dialogue with the payer to find out. Manufacturers are told to prespecify the bias analysis method and validate it with positive controls, which is a proposal, not a threshold anyone must meet.
problems.quote: Although there is considerable interest from the Food and Drug Association in leveraging RWE to expand product indications,9 speciﬁc details of how RWE will inﬂuence CMS drug price negotiations remain less clear.

problems.evidence: Negative controls appear as a supplement to be added when E-values prove too crude, alongside direct adjustment using external information on specific unmeasured confounders. They sit outside the emulation workflow shown in the flowchart, entering only at the branch labeled risk of unmeasured confounding, so nothing makes a proxy or validation analysis a standing component of the design.
problems.quote: To overcome these limitations, E-values should be used with other techniques, such as negative controls26 and direct adjustment using external information on speciﬁc unmeasured or mismeasured confounders.
problems.locator: Applying QBA to Handle Inherent Limitations of RWD

problems.evidence: Clinical equipoise is named as a precondition for causal estimation from real-world data, with the failure case given as a single drug dominating treatment choice. That is a positivity statement, but it is posed as a yes-or-no property of a comparison rather than as a diagnostic that reports which patient histories lack support, and it is offered as a reason the emulation framework can flag infeasible questions rather than as a required output.
problems.quote: The causal estimation of treatments using RWD necessitates clinical equipoise, which may not always be present, for instance, when a single drug is the predominant treatment choice.
problems.locator: Using TTE Techniques to Ensure That Right Comparisons Are Being Made

problems.evidence: The proposed use is comparing etanercept against competing agents across five approved indications, multiple treatment lines and novel sequences, with added benefit to be established across indications, lines and formulations. Nothing defines when two of those uses are the same treatment strategy for the purpose of a single negotiated price, so the equivalence class that the price rests on is left to the analyst.
problems.quote: Thus, to establish added beneﬁts, a comprehensive perspective of the indications, lines, and formulations is needed.

problems.evidence: The flowchart sends studies with more than one eligible time zero to sequential emulation and studies comparing initiators against noninitiators to cloning, censoring and weighting, and then moves on. Neither branch mentions how uncertainty is to be computed after a person is duplicated across sequences or clones, which is the step a payer would need in order to read the confidence interval attached to a price-relevant effect.
problems.quote: When time 0 is not uniquely deﬁned, a 3-step approach may be used, which includes cloning, censoring, and weighting to emulate the target trial; however, other approaches exist.15
problems.locator: Using TTE Techniques to Ensure That Right Comparisons Are Being Made

papers.title: Flexible Approaches Based on Multistate Models and Microsimulation to Perform Real-World Cost-Effectiveness Analyses: An Application to Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin-Kexin Type 9 Inhibitors.
papers.one_line: A cost-effectiveness emulation in Italian electronic health records reduced 96,886 screened subjects to 1976 eligible and 161 PCSK9 inhibitor initiators, then reported a hazard ratio of 0.14 (95% CI 0.07 to 0.27) for all-cause death, far larger than the trial effect, and a lifetime ICER of 29,540 Euro per life year.
papers.what_was_done: A target trial emulation for cost-effectiveness in a regional Italian electronic health record system, combining a flexible parametric multistate disease model with continuous microsimulation. Of 96,886 subjects with at least one LDL measurement between 1 July 2017 and 31 December 2020, 1976 (2%) met an eligibility criterion and 161 (8% of those) were prescribed a PCSK9 inhibitor; median follow-up was 34 months. Inverse probability of treatment weights were fitted by gradient boosting on demographics, Charlson index, prior atherosclerotic disease, diabetes with organ damage, statin history and eligibility date, after which 26% of the study cohort was excluded for propensity scores indicating positivity violations. The seven-state multistate model rejected the Markov assumption in favor of a clock-reset timescale plus a time-varying first-versus-later hospitalization covariate, selected by AIC and BIC and checked against nonparametric cumulative hazards. Treatment effects were a hazard ratio of 0.79 (95% CI 0.63 to 0.99) toward first hospitalization and 0.14 (95% CI 0.07 to 0.27) toward death; microsimulation over a lifetime horizon with 1000 individuals per strategy across 500 probabilistic sensitivity samples gave an ICER of 29,540 Euro per life year (95% CI 23,773 to 38,949), rising to 58,000 Euro per life year under a weaker mortality effect. Time zero was the first prescription date for treated subjects and the eligibility date for comparators.

future_research.gap: Extension of the disease and cost model framework to other settings and to finer patient profiles is left open.
future_research.quote: Moreover, it could be possible to consider scenarios in which it is of interest to examine CE based on more detailed subject proﬁles, allowing for personalized analyses.

problems.evidence: A population-wide electronic health record source with 96,886 screened subjects yielded 1976 eligible people, of whom only 161 initiated the drug, and a further 26% of the cohort was dropped for positivity violations. The lifetime ICER, its confidence interval and every subgroup result rest on that residue, yet the analysis reports database size rather than the effective sample carrying the estimate.
problems.quote: We extracted data related to 96 886 subjects with at least 1 measure of LDL available in the enrollment period

problems.evidence: Positivity is handled by deleting a quarter of the cohort on the basis of estimated propensity score values, and the deletion is reported as a percentage. Which clinical histories fell outside the support of the 161 treated subjects is never stated, so a reader cannot tell whether the surviving estimand covers the patients for whom the reimbursement decision is being made.
problems.quote: Individuals with estimated propensity scores indicating potential violations of the positivity assumption were excluded from the diagnostics and subsequent analysis (26% of the study cohort).
problems.locator: Results, Disease Model, Cost, and Utility Model

problems.evidence: Time zero is set at the first prescription for treated subjects but at the date of satisfying eligibility for comparators, so the two arms enter follow-up at structurally different points in their disease course. No outcome-blind rule justified this asymmetry; the stated defense is that for this drug class prescription follows eligibility closely under Italian guidelines, which is a clinical judgment rather than a procedure, and the mortality hazard ratio of 0.14 is exactly the quantity such an asymmetry would inflate.
problems.quote: Time zero was assumed for individuals treated with PCSK9-I as the date of the ﬁrst prescription and for the comparator group as the date at which the patients satisﬁed all the eligibility criteria.

problems.evidence: The emulated mortality effect (HR 0.14) is many times larger than the trial effect for the same drug class, and the discrepancy is reported as a narrative observation attributed partly to higher baseline cardiovascular risk and partly to possible unmeasured confounding. No calibrated comparison of the two estimands is attempted, and the lifetime ICER of 29,540 Euro per life year is carried forward on the emulated effect rather than on a reconciled one.
problems.quote: the treatment effect of the drug on the risk of death estimated in our study was much higher than the one observed in the RCTs

problems.evidence: Four sensitivity analyses are run and each perturbs one thing: extrapolation beyond observed follow-up, nonadherence, unmeasured confounding through E-values, and utilities. The unmeasured-confounding scenario is constructed by moving the mortality hazard ratio toward a meta-analytic value while leaving the positivity exclusions, the time-zero asymmetry and the measurement of hospitalization costs untouched, so the joint consequence of the violations that are simultaneously present is never estimated.
problems.quote: Therefore, in another sensitivity analysis, we assessed how the estimate for the ICER changed according to different scenarios of unmeasured confounding resulting in a treatment effect of PCSK9-I on death closer to the one reported in a meta-analysis.

problems.evidence: The nuisance models that generate every simulated trajectory are selected by AIC and BIC and validated by comparing predicted cumulative hazards with nonparametric estimates. Both criteria score fit to the observed transition process; neither scores the bias of the causal contrast that the microsimulation then reports, and the model that fit best is also the one that produced the implausible mortality hazard ratio of 0.14.
problems.quote: For model selection, eg, selection of number of degrees of freedom of the baseline transition hazard, Akaike Information Criteria, and Bayesian Information Criteria are used.

papers.title: Introduction to target trial emulation in rehabilitation: a systematic approach to emulate a randomized controlled trial using observational data.
papers.one_line: A Cochrane Rehabilitation methodological consensus paper adapts the seven target trial components to complex rehabilitation interventions and offers the E-value as its only quantitative treatment of residual confounding.
papers.what_was_done: A tutorial produced by participants of the 5th Cochrane Rehabilitation Methodological Meeting, applying the target trial emulation framework to rehabilitation, where blinding and sham comparators are generally unavailable. A worked protocol asks the effect of inpatient stroke rehabilitation delivered through dedicated units versus non-dedicated units on fracture risk within two years in adults aged 65 and over, mapped across eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrasts and analysis plan, and emulated with linked Ontario registry and administrative databases. Confounder selection is directed by causal diagrams; propensity score matching with a balance criterion of standardized mean difference below 10% is given as the worked adjustment method. Residual confounding is addressed only by quantitative bias analysis, specifically the E-value, whose formula is stated as RR plus the square root of RR times RR minus 1. No data are analyzed and no effect estimates are reported. The stated position is that emulation is infeasible when the data source does not measure the components of the rehabilitation program, the outcome or a wide range of confounders.

problems.evidence: The treatment strategies in the worked example are service delivery settings, dedicated versus non-dedicated inpatient stroke rehabilitation units, and nothing defines what makes two units members of the same strategy. Rehabilitation is described as a complex intervention with no valid sham, so the equivalence class of treatment versions is set by the administrative label attached to a unit rather than by any clinical criterion.
problems.quote: For example, if observational data sources do not measure the components of the rehabilitation program or the outcome of interest, we would not be able to emulate the target trial.
problems.locator: Use of observational data for target trial emulation

problems.evidence: The intervention proposed for emulation is an organizational feature of a hospital, and the unit that receives it is a rehabilitation unit while the unit whose outcome is measured is a patient. The framework is transferred wholesale from drug comparisons without addressing the assignment unit or the treatment version, and the acknowledged difficulty of rolling a rehabilitation process out across units over time is offered as a reason to prefer emulation rather than as an identification problem.
problems.quote: Routine practice also does not use placebo/sham or blinding of outcome assessment; thus, studies using target trial emulation in this area emulate pragmatic RCTs of rehabilitation.

problems.evidence: The single quantitative tool offered for unmeasured confounding is the E-value, defined as the minimum association an unmeasured confounder would need with both exposure and outcome to explain the estimate away, conditional on measured covariates. It varies one violated assumption in isolation and says nothing about outcome misclassification of fracture codes, informative loss to follow-up, or the version ambiguity of the rehabilitation exposure, all of which are present at once in the worked design.
problems.quote: E-value is defined as the minimum strength of association (on the risk ratio scale) that an unmeasured confounder would need to have with both the exposure and outcome to fully explain away the observed exposure-outcome association, conditional on measured covariates.
problems.locator: Example of advanced analytic method to achieve comparability of groups at baseline

problems.evidence: The workflow presented for rehabilitation runs from causal diagram to propensity score matching to a balance check to an E-value. Negative control outcomes, proxy variables and validation substudies appear nowhere in the seven components or in the limitations, so a rehabilitation emulation that follows this tutorial has no step at which unmeasured confounding would be probed against external evidence.
problems.quote: Subjects between the two treatment groups can be matched on this propensity score, and balance diagnostics assessed to determine whether there is sufficient balance in baseline covariates (<10% standardized mean difference).
problems.locator: Example of advanced analytic method to achieve comparability of groups at baseline

problems.evidence: Baseline balance is reported as a diagnosable quantity with a numeric threshold of 10%, while exchangeability itself, correct specification of the rehabilitation strategies and completeness of the confounder set are stated as requirements with no reporting device attached. The tutorial places both classes of assumption in the same narrative limitations section, so a reader cannot tell which claims were checked and which were asserted.
problems.quote: It is not possible to emulate the target trial, particularly random assignment, if the observational data used does not measure a wide range of potential confounders or if we do not adjust for identified confounders in the analysis plan.

papers.title: Observational methods for COVID-19 vaccine effectiveness research: an empirical evaluation and target trial emulation.
papers.one_line: Comparing three propensity score methods in 583,813 vaccinated and 332,315 unvaccinated people aged 75 and over, maximum standardized mean differences fell from 0.79 to 0.15 only once general practice was forced into the score, and every method still showed an impossible protective effect in the first 10 days after the first dose.
papers.what_was_done: An empirical head-to-head of overlap weighting, inverse probability of treatment weighting and propensity score matching in UK primary care records (CPRD AURUM), followed by a target trial emulation of the pivotal vaccine trials. All individuals aged 75 and over not previously infected or vaccinated as of 4 January 2021 were included; exposure was a first dose between 4 and 28 January 2021, giving 583,813 vaccinated (348,275 BNT162b2, 235,538 ChAdOx1) and 332,315 unvaccinated. Propensity scores were fitted by lasso with location, age, prior observation time, regional vaccination rates, testing effort and local incidence forced in. Performance metrics were absolute standardized mean differences with a threshold of 0.1, minimum detectable relative risk, and 43 pre-specified negative control outcomes plus PCR testing as a proxy for diagnostic effort, with empirical calibration of hazard ratios against the negative control distribution. Maximum standardized mean difference was 0.79 for inverse probability weighting without location and 0.15 once practice identity was included; overlap weighting retained 905,418 participants against 459,000 and 369,310 in the matched cohorts. Replication was declared when the trial confidence interval overlapped the observational point estimate or the reverse. Effectiveness at 12 weeks was 57% for ChAdOx1 and 75% for BNT162b2. All methods showed a protective association against COVID-19 in the first 10 days after vaccination, before any biological effect is possible.

future_research.gap: Behavioral differences around the time of vaccination that produce the impossible early protective effect are not captured by electronic health records.
future_research.quote: The observed protective vaccine effects shortly after vaccination were in line with previous findings from observational data, 11 , 12 which might be attributable to differences in personal behaviour during the period immediately before and after vaccination, e.g. mask wearing, avoiding crowded indoor places/shielding, rescheduling vaccination if feeling unwell, which unfortunately was unlikely to be captured by electronic health records.

problems.evidence: Replication is decided by a binary overlap rule, and it flips with the outcome definition rather than with the estimand: ChAdOx1 replicated on PCR plus diagnosis but not on PCR alone, and BNT162b2 at 3 weeks failed coverage while showing higher effectiveness than the trial. A calibrated comparison of estimands would have to reconcile symptomatic disease in the trial with a positive test or clinical code in the emulation; the coverage label absorbs that difference instead.
problems.quote: We deemed a trial successfully replicated when the confidence intervals from RCT overlapped with the point estimate from observational data, or vice versa (‘coverage’).

problems.evidence: Forty-three pre-specified negative control outcomes plus a diagnostic-effort proxy are run for every candidate adjustment method, and hazard ratios are empirically calibrated against the negative control distribution, which is the closest thing here to an integrated workflow step. It does not close the entry: the calibrated estimates still show a protective effect in the first 10 days after a first dose, a period in which no effect is biologically possible, so the negative controls detected residual bias they could not remove and the main effectiveness estimates were reported anyway.
problems.quote: Unexpectedly, all tested methods showed a protective effect against the clinical outcomes of PCR+ and PCR+/diagnosis in the first 10 days after first-dose vaccination
problems.locator: Results, Minimizing confounding in vaccine effectiveness research

problems.evidence: Three estimators are compared on the same cohort against balance, power and negative control error, and the choice is shown to matter: maximum standardized mean difference ran from 0.79 to 0.15 depending on how location entered, and matching discarded roughly half a million people that weighting kept. What is supplied is a comparison for one exposure in one database, not a requirement that any study demonstrate its estimator choice was immaterial, and the three methods target different estimands (ATE, ATT and ATO) that are compared as if interchangeable.
problems.quote: Unlike observational studies, RCTs do not distinguish between average treatment effect (ATE), average treatment in the treated (ATT) or average treatment effect in the overlap (ATO).

problems.evidence: Overlap weighting is selected because it balances covariates exactly and retains 905,418 people against 459,000 after matching, and the reported diagnostics are standardized mean differences and minimum detectable relative risks. Neither names the patient histories left unsupported; the practice-level nonoverlap that drove maximum imbalance from 0.79 to 0.15 is visible only as a summary statistic, and the estimand silently becomes an overlap-weighted quantity in a population aged 75 and over.
problems.quote: Including GP practice further reduced confounding, with maximum SMDs decreasing from 0.79 in IPTW-PS base to 0.15 in IPTW-PS gp .
problems.locator: Results, Comparison of model performance to minimize confounding

problems.evidence: The emulation's outcome is a positive PCR or a clinical diagnosis code in primary care records, while the trials measured symptomatic disease; results differed between the two observational definitions, replicating on one and not the other. Structural availability of a COVID-19 variable in the database did not make it the same construct as the trial endpoint, and the difference is acknowledged in the limitations rather than accounted for in the estimate.
problems.quote: Differences in outcome definition, i.e. symptomatic COVID-19 assessed in the trials vs positive test s/clinical diagnoses in our study, are being acknowledged.

problems.evidence: Testing effort had to be forced into the propensity score and PCR testing itself was used as a control outcome, which concedes that healthcare-use variables sit on the path between vaccination and outcome ascertainment. Vaccinated people with BNT162b2 were tested less in the first 10 days than the unvaccinated, so conditioning on the testing process differed by arm at exactly the point where the impossible early protective effect appears.
problems.quote: Diagnostic effort: we used PCR testing, i.e. performed COVID-19 PCR test regardless of test result, in the first 10 days after index date as a control outcome and proxy for diagnostic effort.

papers.title: Using Trial and Observational Data to Assess Effectiveness: Trial Emulation, Transportability, Benchmarking, and Joint Analysis.
papers.one_line: Formal benchmarking of an emulation against a trial is shown to rest on four assumption blocks of which only one is supported by design, and in the worked TASTE example the emulation gave a risk difference of 1.0% while the transported trial gave minus 0.3%.
papers.what_was_done: A review building a framework for benchmarking and jointly analyzing a randomized trial with an observational emulation, combining the target trial framework with transportability methods. An evidence map screened 165 PubMed abstracts to 70 full texts and identified 58 studies as implementations of the framework in the decade to June 2021, spanning 10 in oncology, 8 in infectious disease, 8 in cardiovascular medicine and 32 elsewhere, and 40 comparing medication strategies, 10 procedures, 3 lifestyle modification and 5 other interventions. Across those studies and in most conceptual discussions the target population of the emulation is left implicit, fixed by whoever the eligibility criteria happen to select in the available data. A worked example based on the TASTE trial of thrombus aspiration in myocardial infarction, emulated in the SWEDEHEART registry with one discrete covariate, gives 30-day risk differences of minus 0.2% (95% CI minus 1.0 to 0.6) trial only, 1.0% (95% CI minus 0.1 to 2.2) adjusted emulation, minus 0.3% (95% CI minus 1.1 to 0.6) transported, and 0.0% (95% CI minus 0.7 to 0.6) jointly. Formal benchmarking is shown to require four assumption blocks: no trial engagement effects, hidden versions of treatment or interference; sufficient measured confounders and overlap in the observational data; exchangeability and overlap between trial and emulation populations; and exchangeability within the trial. Only the last is supported by randomization. Measurement error, nonadherence, missing data and incomplete follow-up are assumed away throughout.

future_research.gap: Benchmarking cannot be made an automatic procedure and reduces in practice to epidemiologic judgment.
future_research.quote: To a large extent, then, benchmarking will remain an exercise in epidemiologic judgment, informed by quantitative analyses similar to those we implemented in our example.

future_research.gap: The framework covers only point treatments and binary end-of-study outcomes; sustained strategies and failure-time outcomes need methods not developed here.
future_research.quote: Extensions to study the effects of sustained treatments and more complex outcomes (i.e., longitudinal or failure-time outcomes) are possible and usually necessary in practical applications, but require more specialized methods for design and analysis.
future_research.locator: Example: thrombus aspiration for myocardial infarction

problems.evidence: The review supplies the missing structure for what a benchmark is: the emulation and the transportability analysis target the same estimand under different assumptions, so agreement is evidence and disagreement localizes the failure to one or the other. What it does not supply is any extrapolation rule. When the two disagree, the data cannot say which assumption failed, and the relative plausibility has to be judged case by case, so a successful benchmark on one question licenses nothing about the next.
problems.quote: If the analyses disagree, however, the data cannot determine which assumption fails to hold.

problems.evidence: Replication is replaced by a quantitative comparison on a common scale: in the worked example the adjusted emulation gives a 30-day risk difference of 1.0% (95% CI minus 0.1 to 2.2) against a transported trial estimate of minus 0.3% (95% CI minus 1.1 to 0.6) for the same target population, with a joint estimate of 0.0%. That is a calibrated comparison rather than a label. It stops short of a calibration procedure that survives contact with practice: high-dimensional covariates make the implied equality hard to test, and failing to reject is stated not to mean the assumption holds.
problems.quote: Though this implication can be verified in the data, we caution that formal statistical testing is likely to be challenging in realistic applications with high dimensional covariates.
problems.locator: Joint analysis of the index trial and the emulation

problems.evidence: The assumption inventory for transporting an estimate is stated in full and only one of its four blocks comes from randomization. Sampling assumptions, meaning exchangeability and overlap between the trial and emulation populations, are stacked on top of the confounding assumptions inside the observational analysis, and measurement error, nonadherence and incomplete follow-up are excluded from the accounting altogether.
problems.quote: Only the last item in this list is directly supported by trial design.

problems.evidence: Hidden versions of treatment sit in the first assumption block of formal benchmarking, alongside interference and trial engagement effects, and the review assumes them away rather than testing them. In a comparison of percutaneous intervention with and without thrombus aspiration across a trial protocol and routine registry care, the versions of the procedure delivered in the two settings are exactly the quantity that no defined equivalence class covers.
problems.quote: In our description of formal benchmarking, we assumed 1) the absence of trial engagement effects, hidden versions of treatment, or interference;

problems.evidence: Across the 58 studies mapped, the target population of the emulation is left implicit and determined by whoever survives the eligibility criteria in the available data. That is the mismatch between the scientific target and the emulated protocol going unnamed at the level of an entire literature, so no decomposition of the resulting loss is even possible from what those studies report.
problems.quote: In most conceptual discussions of the target trial framework and across the studies in our evidence map, the target population of the emulation is left implicit, determined by applying eligibility criteria to the population underlying the observational data.
problems.locator: The target population in the target trial framework

problems.evidence: Covariates, treatments and outcomes are assumed to be similarly defined and measured across the trial and the registry, which is what permits measurement error to be ignored in the benchmarking algebra. In the worked example a trial-ascertained 30-day outcome is compared with a registry-ascertained one and the two are treated as the same variable, so any phenotype error is absorbed into the disagreement that the framework then attributes to confounding or to effect modification.
problems.quote: Furthermore, we assumed throughout that covariates, treatments, and outcomes are similarly defined and measured across designs, allowing us to ignore measurement error issues

problems.evidence: Some violation of the four assumption blocks is stated to be practically inevitable, and the response offered is judgment possibly informed by sensitivity analyses about whether the violations are small enough for the comparison to mean anything. No joint sensitivity analysis over confounding, transport, versions of treatment and measurement is proposed, so the simultaneous case is handled by declaring it a matter for expertise.
problems.quote: Furthermore, given that some degree of violation of these assumptions is practically inevitable, judgment—possibly informed by sensitivity analyses (126)— will be needed to determine whether the violations are small enough that a quantitative comparison of the emulation and transportability analyses is meaningful and can be interpreted in a useful way.

problems.evidence: The worked example is deliberately run with a single discrete covariate so that fully saturated models can be used, and the review states that with realistic high-dimensional covariates modeling restrictions become necessary and misspecification can bias the result even when every causal assumption holds. The remedy is a pointer to doubly robust and data-adaptive methods, with no criterion for choosing among them and no requirement that a study show the choice was immaterial.
problems.quote: In practice, however, the covariates will often be high dimensional and investigators will need to impose some modeling restrictions (135). In such cases, model misspecification can introduce bias, even if the causal assumptions hold.
